pairs.subject: quality-gates
pairs.evidence: clients/typescript/test/conformance.test.ts:61 When the spec is missing, the conformance test tells the reader to run `just clients`. That recipe is `node scripts/gen/generate-clients.mjs`, which reads clients/openapi.json and itself exits 2 with "clients/openapi.json is missing". The remedy, applied as worded, cannot clear the check; the real producer is `just openapi`.

techniques.evidence: clients/typescript/test/conformance.test.ts:61 Names a recipe that consumes the missing file instead of producing it. scripts/gen/generate-clients.mjs:213-218 names the correct producer (UPDATE_OPENAPI=1 cargo test ... spec_snapshot, i.e. `just openapi`).

clients/typescript/test/conformance.test.ts:70 A schema with no direct properties (e.g. one reshaped into allOf/$ref) yields zero required fields, and assertFixtureCoversSchema then passes having checked nothing. Nothing asserts the property set is non-empty. Latent: today RecordDto/RevisionDto/RevisionPageDto have 7/13/2 properties.

clients/typescript/test/conformance.test.ts:80 Required fields come from the served openapi.json, not a hand-typed list, so a field added on the server side reddens the test. The intermediate document is itself pinned to the live router by a Rust test.
clients/typescript/test/conformance.test.ts:13 The header states the one question this instrument answers (fixture shape agreement) and explicitly disclaims the end-to-end HTTP wiring question.

pairs.subject: quality-gates
pairs.evidence: crates/core/src/catalog.rs:344 Contract range checks drop any record whose ranged field is non-numeric before comparing. A contract that declares `ranges` without a matching `types` entry passes such values with no violation and no skip count. The test at catalog.rs:1328 pins that silent pass.

techniques.evidence: crates/core/src/catalog.rs:344 A record the range condition cannot evaluate is silently excluded, neither failed nor reported as a counted skip. The design delegates to `types` (line 251), but nothing announces how many records went unevaluated.
crates/core/src/catalog.rs:673 Warn vs Block is decided by the enforce flag in ContractVerdict::from_violations, and the status surface says in words when the label gates nothing.
crates/core/tests/lane_artifact/mod.rs:20 A lane that failed to write its artifact panics, so it cannot read as a lane that passed.
crates/core/src/catalog.rs:421 A misspelled cadence used to be evaluated into 'no freshness expectation', making the rule unfireable. It is now refused at parse time by vocabulary_findings.
crates/core/src/catalog.rs:213 One freshness_window_secs function feeds both /catalog/health and /sources, so the two surfaces cannot judge staleness differently.

pairs.subject: quality-gates
pairs.evidence: crates/core/tests/error_cause_chain.rs:64 The cause-flattening guard compares only the count of found sites (keyed `path:line`) against the length of EXPECTED_FLATTENED, whose entries are prose labels never matched against those keys. Fixing one waived extract.rs site while adding a new flattening site elsewhere keeps the count equal and stays green.

techniques.evidence: crates/core/tests/error_cause_chain.rs:64 The waivers are a count, not identities. No entry is matched to a found site, so substituting one finding for another passes, and a mistyped entry is never reported.
crates/core/tests/error_cause_chain.rs:228 The detector keys on the binding name. Renaming `e` to `x` keeps the flattening and clears the check, and the verdict does not state that limit.

crates/core/tests/error_cause_chain.rs:192 A call the matcher cannot balance is skipped with `continue`, not reported. Alternative spellings (aliased imports, whitespace before the paren) are neither recognised nor banned, in a tree the repo owns.
crates/core/tests/error_cause_chain.rs:82 A paired positive-control floor proves the same scanner still finds sites, so an empty walk or an unreadable crate cannot pass as clean.

crates/core/tests/error_cause_chain.rs:189 Comment lines naming the banned shape are normalised out, so prose cannot satisfy or trip the matcher. Partial: string literals and inline block comments are not blanked.
crates/core/tests/error_cause_chain.rs:70 The failure names an in-tree constructor and the in-file allowlist, both reachable from where the reader stands.
crates/core/tests/error_cause_chain.rs:12 The 'attach the cause' convention is mechanised as a test rather than left as prose.
crates/core/tests/error_cause_chain.rs:227 The rule is local to one call expression, so a window-sized pattern can decide it without a call graph.
crates/core/src/error.rs:1669 Terminal classification is an exhaustive match, so a new variant fails compilation. Its blocking status comes from construction, not from a label.

crates/core/tests/store_instrument_chokepoint.rs:6 The store chokepoint is declared a partial measurement census (StoreOp::ALL), not a routing invariant. It deliberately makes no claim that every statement passes through it, so the bijection precondition does not hold.
